project_ideas.name: Desktop Pool Isolation and Cost Harness
project_ideas.poc: A virtual desktop pool manager that provisions disposable isolated desktops driven by a cross-OS scripting API, runs N agents in parallel on perturbed task variants, and deliberately attempts cross-environment state leakage and resource exhaustion to probe isolation boundaries.

project_ideas.based_on: The Record -> Replay -> Break -> Heal loop turns a captured execution into a durable skill
project_ideas.hypothesis: Repeated break/heal cycles on a recorded skill converge in the first few iterations but drift semantically afterwards, so task correctness stays high while the rewritten skill's diff grows and its behavioral surface diverges from the original recording.
project_ideas.measurement: Task correctness per cycle, diff size of the rewritten skill per cycle, and semantic divergence measured by re-running the healed skill unperturbed and comparing action sequences to the original recording.
project_ideas.name: Skill Heal Drift Tracker
project_ideas.poc: A loop that records a desktop task as a skill, replays it, injects a controlled perturbation, lets the agent rewrite the skill, and versions each healed artifact — running until either the diff stabilizes or the original task semantics fail.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Ang Li
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Building full-stack infrastructure for computer use agents using a neuro-symbolic approach (Agent S, Simulang, and Saibox).
  • Purpose: To provide technical insight into computer use agents, introduce the Simular infrastructure stack for CUA development, and discuss the future of AI-driven computer automation. Ang Li, co-founder and CEO of Simular, discusses the evolution and engineering of computer use agents over the past two years. He explores the challenges of autonomy and computer operation, the shift from VLM-only agents to neuro-symbolic architectures (combining VLM perception with coding agents), and introduces the infrastructure stack built by Simular: Agent S, Simulang CLI, and Saibox virtual computer cloud.

Topic Map

Background and Evolution of Computer Use Agents

  • Explanation: Speaker's background in deep learning (PhD, DeepMind) and the evolution of AI agents from comparative programming to neural networks and autonomous computer use.
  • Key claims:
    • General AI systems need to be neuro-symbolic, combining code and neural nets.
    • Computer use agents represent a broader category than API-based agents because they operate full desktop environments without requiring APIs.
  • Examples:
    • Attempting to use GPT-4V with PyAutoGUI in late 2023 to click iMessage icon, which required iterative refinement and often failed due to VLM brittleness.
  • Terminology:
    • AGI
    • neuro-symbolic
    • computer use agents (CUA)
  • Why it matters: Establishes why computer use agents are harder than standard API agents and motivates the need for specialized infrastructure.

The Two Core Problems: Autonomy and Computer

  • Explanation: Breaking down autonomous computer agents into two fundamental components: Autonomy (reasoning, planning, recovery) and Computer (operating desktop, browser, apps, terminal).
  • Key claims:
    • Autonomy is neuro-symbolic: VLM agent handles novelty, coding agent handles execution.
    • Computer interaction requires robust perception and grounding across multiple signals.
  • Examples:
    • Comparing self-driving cars (steering wheel to mouse/keyboard, lidar/radar/camera to screenshot/accessibility tree/DOM tree).
  • Terminology:
    • VLM agent
    • coding agent
    • accessibility tree
    • DOM tree
    • grounding
  • Why it matters: Provides a clear taxonomy for understanding what makes autonomous computer agents succeed or fail.

Agent S: Architecture and Scaling

  • Explanation: Evolution of Agent S from late 2024 (accessibility tree, ID-based grounding, memory management, 'harness') to early 2025 (Agent S2, vision-only multi-layer architecture) and late 2025 (Agent S3, inference time scaling).
  • Key claims:
    • Combining two foundation models inside the same harness outperforms single models.
    • Reliability decays with every repeat in perturbed environments, but clarification and scaling test-time compute improve success rates.
  • Examples:
    • MacBook agent controlled by FaceTime winning Cal Hacks grand prize.
  • Terminology:
    • Agent S
    • OSWorld benchmark
    • inference time scaling
    • pass@k
    • pass^k
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates how architectural iterations and evaluation metrics drive state-of-the-art performance in OS task execution.

Simulang and Saibox: The Open Source CLI and Cloud Infrastructure

  • Explanation: Introduction of Simulang (scriptable language for running scripts that operate computers) and Saibox (virtual computer cloud for scalable agent execution).
  • Key claims:
    • Simulang brings Playwright-like scripting to the entire desktop across major operating systems.
    • Saibox provides scalable, isolated virtual desktop infrastructure for running hundreds of agents in parallel.
  • Examples:
    • Live demo using Claude Code with Simulang to open website and summarize events.
  • Terminology:
    • Simulang
    • Saibox
    • sapi
    • virtual desktop
  • Why it matters: Provides developers with concrete open-source tools and cloud infrastructure to build and scale computer use agents.

Key Points

Neuro-symbolic integration is necessary for general AI

  • Explanation: Combining neural networks (VLMs for perception and handling novelty) with symbolic systems (code for deterministic execution) creates robust agents.
  • Evidence: Agent S architecture combining VLM agents with coding agents.
  • Practical implication: Developers should not rely solely on VLMs or hardcoded scripts; combining them yields higher reliability.

Perception requires multiple signals

  • Explanation: Relying on a single signal like screenshots is insufficient; agents need screenshots, accessibility trees, and DOM trees combined.
  • Evidence: OSWorld benchmark results comparing single-signal vs multi-signal perception.
  • Practical implication: Agent frameworks must incorporate OS-level accessibility APIs alongside visual understanding.

Reliability decays with repetition without clarification

  • Explanation: When running tasks repeatedly in perturbed environments, agent success rates drop unless instructed to ask clarification questions.
  • Evidence: Research paper 'On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents' showing drop from Pass@1 to Pass^3.
  • Practical implication: Prompt agents to seek clarification on ambiguous instructions to maintain high reliability.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Neuro-Symbolic Agent Architecture

  • How it works: Pairs a VLM agent for open-ended perception and handling novelty with a coding agent for deterministic, repeatable step execution.
  • Components:
    • VLM agent (perception, general reasoning)
    • Coding agent (deterministic execution, code generation)
    • Memory management and harness layer
  • When to use: When building agents that need to operate arbitrary desktop applications and web browsers autonomously.

Record -> Replay -> Break -> Heal

  • How it works: Record task execution as a skill, replay it, deliberately break the environment, and let the agent heal by rewriting the skill in real-time.
  • Components:
    • Record (capture skill)
    • Replay (watch reasoning)
    • Break (perturb environment)
    • Heal (recover and rewrite code)
  • When to use: When building robust, self-improving automation scripts on desktops.

Examples & Case Studies

Building a MacBook agent controlled via FaceTime at Cal Hacks.

  • Illustrates: Multimodal agent with full control over a computer via voice and video interaction.
  • Lesson: Users can interact with computer use agents remotely through natural communication interfaces.

Using Simulang to write a script that opens the AI Engineer World's Fair website and summarizes speaker schedules.

  • Illustrates: Running scriptable desktop automation using Node.js and Simulang CLI.
  • Lesson: Developers can automate complex desktop workflows using plain TypeScript and accessibility snapshots.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Check out Simulang on GitHub (github.com/simular-ai/simulang).
    • Explore Saibox virtual computer cloud via sai.work/api.
    • Use invitation code AIEWF2026 to start building.
  • Strategic:
    • Combine VLM flexibility with code determinism to achieve higher agent reliability.
    • Use multi-signal perception (screenshots, accessibility trees, DOM trees) for robust UI grounding.
    • Implement clarification prompting to maintain reliability across repeated task executions.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How can security guardrails be effectively enforced at the OS level for computer use agents?
    • What are the scaling economics of running thousands of virtual desktops for cloud-managed agent fleets?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Agent S achieved 20% success rate on OSWorld in late 2024, winning best paper at ICLR 2025 Agentic AI workshop. (benchmark performance)
  • Clarification prompting increases reliability and jumps success rates across repeated task executions. (experimental finding)

Notable Quotes

"The general AI system needs to be neuro-symbolic, basically code combined with neural nets." "Two words, two hard problems. You have to solve both: Autonomy and Computer."

Compressed Summary

  • Autonomous computer agents require both autonomy and computer operation capabilities.
  • Neuro-symbolic architectures combine VLM perception with coding agents for stability and adaptability.
  • Simulang provides an open-source CLI for scriptable computer automation in TypeScript.
  • Saibox delivers scalable virtual desktop infrastructure for running agent fleets in the cloud.
  • Keywords: agents, infrastructure, neuro-symbolic, desktop, automation
  • Core insight: Building reliable computer use agents requires fusing neural perception with deterministic code execution within scalable virtual desktop infrastructure.

- **Explanation**: Breaking down autonomous computer agents into two fundamental components: Autonomy (reasoning, planning, recovery) and Computer (operating desktop, browser, apps, terminal).
- **Key claims**:
  - Autonomy is neuro-symbolic: VLM agent handles novelty, coding agent handles execution.
  - Computer interaction requires robust perception and grounding across multiple signals.
- **Examples**:
  - Comparing self-driving cars (steering wheel to mouse/keyboard, lidar/radar/camera to screenshot/accessibility tree/DOM tree).
- **Terminology**:
  - VLM agent
  - coding agent
  - accessibility tree
  - DOM tree
  - grounding
- **Why it matters**: Provides a clear taxonomy for understanding what makes autonomous computer agents succeed or fail.
### Agent S: Architecture and Scaling
- **Explanation**: Evolution of Agent S from late 2024 (accessibility tree, ID-based grounding, memory management, 'harness') to early 2025 (Agent S2, vision-only multi-layer architecture) and late 2025 (Agent S3, inference time scaling).
- **Key claims**:
  - Combining two foundation models inside the same harness outperforms single models.
  - Reliability decays with every repeat in perturbed environments, but clarification and scaling test-time compute improve success rates.
- **Examples**:
  - MacBook agent controlled by FaceTime winning Cal Hacks grand prize.
- **Terminology**:
  - Agent S
  - OSWorld benchmark
  - inference time scaling
  - pass@k
  - pass^k
- **Why it matters**: Demonstrates how architectural iterations and evaluation metrics drive state-of-the-art performance in OS task execution.
### Simulang and Saibox: The Open Source CLI and Cloud Infrastructure
- **Explanation**: Introduction of Simulang (scriptable language for running scripts that operate computers) and Saibox (virtual computer cloud for scalable agent execution).
- **Key claims**:
  - Simulang brings Playwright-like scripting to the entire desktop across major operating systems.
  - Saibox provides scalable, isolated virtual desktop infrastructure for running hundreds of agents in parallel.
- **Examples**:
  - Live demo using Claude Code with Simulang to open website and summarize events.
- **Terminology**:
  - Simulang
  - Saibox
  - sapi
  - virtual desktop
- **Why it matters**: Provides developers with concrete open-source tools and cloud infrastructure to build and scale computer use agents.
## Key Points
### Neuro-symbolic integration is necessary for general AI
- **Explanation**: Combining neural networks (VLMs for perception and handling novelty) with symbolic systems (code for deterministic execution) creates robust agents.
- **Evidence**: Agent S architecture combining VLM agents with coding agents.
- **Practical implication**: Developers should not rely solely on VLMs or hardcoded scripts; combining them yields higher reliability.
### Perception requires multiple signals
- **Explanation**: Relying on a single signal like screenshots is insufficient; agents need screenshots, accessibility trees, and DOM trees combined.
- **Evidence**: OSWorld benchmark results comparing single-signal vs multi-signal perception.
- **Practical implication**: Agent frameworks must incorporate OS-level accessibility APIs alongside visual understanding.
### Reliability decays with repetition without clarification
- **Explanation**: When running tasks repeatedly in perturbed environments, agent success rates drop unless instructed to ask clarification questions.
- **Evidence**: Research paper 'On the Reliability of Computer Use Agents' showing drop from Pass@1 to Pass^3.
- **Practical implication**: Prompt agents to seek clarification on ambiguous instructions to maintain high reliability.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Neuro-Symbolic Agent Architecture
- **How it works**: Pairs a VLM agent for open-ended perception and handling novelty with a coding agent for deterministic, repeatable step execution.
- **Components**:
  - VLM agent (perception, general reasoning)
  - Coding agent (deterministic execution, code generation)
  - Memory management and harness layer
- **When to use**: When building agents that need to operate arbitrary desktop applications and web browsers autonomously.
### Record -> Replay -> Break -> Heal
- **How it works**: Record task execution as a skill, replay it, deliberately break the environment, and let the agent heal by rewriting the skill in real-time.
- **Components**:
  - Record (capture skill)
  - Replay (watch reasoning)
  - Break (perturb environment)
  - Heal (recover and rewrite code)
- **When to use**: When building robust, self-improving automation scripts on desktops.
## Examples & Case Studies
### Building a MacBook agent controlled via FaceTime at Cal Hacks.
- **Illustrates**: Multimodal agent with full control over a computer via voice and video interaction.
- **Lesson**: Users can interact with computer use agents remotely through natural communication interfaces.
### Using Simulang to write a script that opens the AI Engineer World's Fair website and summarizes speaker schedules.
- **Illustrates**: Running scriptable desktop automation using Node.js and Simulang CLI.
- **Lesson**: Developers can automate complex desktop workflows using plain TypeScript and accessibility snapshots.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Check out Simulang on GitHub (github.com/simular-ai/simulang).
  - Explore Saibox virtual computer cloud via sai.work/api.
  - Use invitation code AIEWF2026 to start building.
- **Strategic**:
  - Combine VLM flexibility with code determinism to achieve higher agent reliability.
  - Use multi-signal perception (screenshots, accessibility trees, DOM trees) for robust UI grounding.
  - Implement clarification prompting to maintain reliability across repeated task executions.
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - How can security guardrails be effectively enforced at the OS level for computer use agents?
  - What are the scaling economics of running thousands of virtual desktops for cloud-managed agent fleets?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- Agent S achieved 20% success rate on OSWorld in late 2024, winning best paper at ICLR 2025 Agentic AI workshop. (benchmark performance)
- Clarification prompting increases reliability and jumps success rates across repeated task executions. (experimental finding)
## Notable Quotes
> "The general AI system needs to be neuro-symbolic, basically code combined with neural nets."
> "Two words, two hard problems. You have to solve both: Autonomy and Computer."
## Compressed Summary
- Autonomous computer agents require both autonomy and computer operation capabilities.
- Neuro-symbolic architectures combine VLM perception with coding agents for stability and adaptability.
- Simulang provides an open-source CLI for scriptable computer automation in TypeScript.
- Saibox delivers scalable virtual desktop infrastructure for running agent fleets in the cloud.
- **Keywords**: agents, infrastructure, neuro-symbolic, desktop, automation
- **Core insight**: Building reliable computer use agents requires fusing neural perception with deterministic code execution within scalable virtual desktop infrastructure.
